findings.breaking_input: Tag v1.2.3 pushed while CHANGELOG.md has a heading like `## [1.2.3] - 2026-10-24`, plus an earlier heading `## [1.2.30]`. awk matches via index($0,h)==1 with h='## [1.2.3]' which requires the closing bracket, fine; but CRLF CHANGELOG.md (written on a Windows box) makes the section lines carry a trailing CR, and a CRLF `package.json` is irrelevant. The notes file then holds CR-terminated lines.
findings.why: Release notes get stray CRs; more importantly a prerelease tag such as v1.2.3-rc.1 yields ver='1.2.3-rc.1', which fails the package.json equality check with an opaque error, and a tag like v1.2.3 pushed on a commit not on main is released without any check that the tagged commit is reachable from main.
findings.fix: Strip CR from CHANGELOG with `tr -d '\r'` before awk, and verify the tag commit is an ancestor of origin/main (`git merge-base --is-ancestor`) before publishing.
findings.twin_of: (m) A one-line count file accepts `\r\n` as well as `\n`

findings.breaking_input: A `.count` file that is empty, or whose first line is non-numeric (e.g. `TODO`, or a UTF-8 BOM followed by `12`). The new awk uses `FNR==1{s+=$1}`.
findings.why: A BOM makes `$1` read as `\ufeff12`, which awk coerces to 0, silently deflating the claimed total so a shrunken lane passes. A non-numeric first line also coerces to 0 with no error. The old `cat` path had the same weakness, but the fix claims to validate per file and does not.
findings.fix: Have awk reject any file whose first field does not match /^[0-9]+$/ (after stripping CR and BOM) and exit non-zero, so a malformed claim is red rather than 0.
findings.twin_of: (o) A claimed count (`.count`, a drop row) is checked against what actually ran or existed

findings.breaking_input: `find ... -exec awk '...' {} +` with many .count files: find batches arguments and may invoke awk more than once (large argument list, Windows command-line length limit).
findings.why: Each awk invocation prints its own `END` sum, so the command substitution holds several lines such as `19` and `4`; `[ "$ran" -ge "$claimed" ]` then fails with `integer expression expected` on a multi-line value, or the echo shows the wrong total. The same applies to the identical line in ci.yml.
findings.fix: Pipe the find output through a second awk that sums the partial totals, or use `-exec awk ... {} \;` per file with a summing outer awk, so exactly one number reaches the comparison.
findings.twin_of: (al) Numbers read from several files are summed per file, never through `cat`

findings.breaking_input: `node --test --test-reporter=tap "tests/**/*.test.mjs"` on windows-latest where the quoted glob is passed to node unexpanded.
findings.why: Glob expansion is delegated to node, whose support for `**` depends on the Node version. If it matches fewer files than `.count` dirs imply, the run is only caught by the aggregate check; the claimed set (depth exactly 2) and the executed set (any depth) still come from two enumerations.
findings.fix: Build one file list with `find tests -name '*.test.mjs' -type f` and pass it to node, deriving the claim from the same list's directories.
findings.twin_of: (k) A counted file set and the set the runner executes come from ONE enumeration

findings.breaking_input: A push containing `initiatives/ci/x.md` together with a file whose test mapping is empty but which `isPaperwork` rejects, e.g. a `.github/workflows/weekly.yml` change that no test names.
findings.why: `notes` requires every path to be paperwork or a lane note, so a mixed push stays 'no test file mapped' (exit 1) correctly; but a lane note under a nested evidence path with a single segment such as `initiatives/ci/README.md` is also treated as paperwork even when a bats gate reads it by glob, so a break in it exits 0 locally and is red only on CI.
findings.fix: Restrict the regex to the named allow-list (`debt-ledger.md`, `fixed-defects.md`) instead of every `*.md` directly under a lane.
findings.twin_of: (v) An allowlist of "safe to skip" paths also asks the tests' own text
